executiveSummary: GM1895 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 39,586-person municipality control, 50 neighbourhoods in eleven districts, sixteen BAG places, 42 BRT settlements, three conventional rail stations, 111 scheduled-transit stop areas and four domestic NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 39,595, only nine above the separately published control (+0.023%). Drieborg's BAG label point falls just outside the independently generalized CBS boundary and must remain a geometry-edition caveat, not be silently discarded. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oldambt combines the Dollard primary sea defence, Eemskanaal-Dollard and Oldambt boezems, deeply drained clay/peat polders, the 830-hectare Oldambtmeer, gas/salt/peat-related subsidence, induced seismicity, forests and a remnant high-peat island, extensive agriculture, the A7/rail German-border axis and the regional Ommelander hospital at Scheemda. Coastal-flood reports a generic legacy inundation amplitude of 1.212376 from T+6 through T+24, 14,051 affected resident-equivalents and 346,751.641 deprived person-hours at T+24 without selecting a Dollard level/wave boundary, dike section/state, breach/overtopping case, connected LIWO footprint, arrival or recession. Direct amplitude becomes zero at T+48, yet 14,517 remain affected, before T+72 is labelled recovering. The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset correctly gives zero direct impact; retain that narrowly scoped suppression while leaving Eems/Dollard, boezem, polder, pluvial and groundwater pathways separately Unknown until selected. Pluvial reports 0.236408 at T+12/T+24 without event-valid rain, terrain, soil, pump, boezem, groundwater or crop state. Earthquake reports 0.080038 g and 4,476 affected at T+6 without a named event, shake grid, soil or building-vulnerability case. Eight unrelated active presets reuse a Winschoten-population-led neighbourhood order, while a controlled T+24 wildfire source at the official Meerland centre ranks its containing high-peat neighbourhood 32nd of 50. Public context identifies 278 assigned water/wastewater objects, a local Nieuwe Statenzijl Waterinfo point, one Enexis planning sample, 137 antennas, 28 education uses and the 24/7 Ommelander emergency department, but none establishes complete live topology, capacity, backup, staffing or restoration. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, historic conditions, planning values and static register status must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1895 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region data
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM1895 as Oldambt in Groningen and safety region Groningen and report 39,586 residents, density 175/km², 26.4% aged 65 or older and 7,301 one-person households; the generated centre [7.066055489135063,53.18909050586359] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Fifty neighbourhood rows in eleven districts sum to 39,595 residents, nine above the separately rounded municipality control (+0.023%); households sum to 18,920 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 10,425. Model allocation reconciles to the control without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies sixteen places and BRT supplies 42 source-labelled settlements: nineteen woonkernen, seven deelkernen, three gehuchten and thirteen buurtschappen. Drieborg's BAG label point lies outside the independently versioned generalized CBS boundary; this is a review caveat, not proof of foreign membership.

CBS regional statistics expose 36 fields. District heating and public charging are null in all 50 rows; cars per household is null in eight and several housing/benefit fields in two. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; null/suppression remains NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027, Oldambt/Fiemel and current Dollarddijk strengthening
evidenceSources.edition: Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027; current Dollarddijk project status inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Oldambt/Fiemel is an open agricultural clay/peat area adjoining the Eems-Dollard, largely pumped polders with separate boezem systems. Rozema and Fiemel pumps discharge to the Eems-Dollard; locally lowest ground northeast of Nieuwolda toward Woldendorp is about 3 m below NAP while settlement ridges can reach about 5 m above NAP.

The programme describes roughly 22 km of sea dike in Oldambt/Fiemel, Oldambtmeer as possible Eemskanaal-Dollard-boezem storage, and continuing subsidence from gas extraction, salt extraction and peat oxidation. It states the regional boezem defences were assessed/strengthened and earthquake-resistant in that programme context; that is not a perpetual or event-time guarantee.

Current project information at https://www.hunzeenaas.nl/projecten/versterken-dollarddijk/ says the 2017–2023 assessment found the full Hunze en Aa's sea-defence area does not yet meet future statutory standards and identifies the 15 km Dollarddijk between Punt van Reide and the German border as the first strengthening section. Future-standard non-compliance does not itself mean imminent failure.

The authority identifies urban pluvial and groundwater nuisance, clay vulnerability to peak rainfall and long-running peat-oxidation subsidence. Its PDF/project pages are public planning evidence; no standard redistribution licence, machine event feed or guaranteed cadence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 Oldambt candidate catalogue and Nieuwe Statenzijl Waterinfo context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; public WFS queried 3 September 2026; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: The bounded LIWO WFS returns three primary candidates and 21 regional candidates. Polygon testing against the generated boundary contains primary candidates 639 Carel Coenraadpolder and 640 west of Nieuwe Statenzijl, plus eighteen regional candidates labelled Eemskanaal-Dollardboezem or Oldambt; bbox results outside the polygon were not assigned.

Candidate points and frequency-class flags are scenario-selection metadata, not active breaches, forecasts, connected inundation footprints or local depths. A causal use must pin LIWO release, scenario/model dates, water boundary and datum, defence/breach/control, probability/context, footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/duration/recession, CRS/resolution/units, uncertainty, coverage, NoData, licence and expert approval.

The deployment has one local Nieuwe Statenzijl, Dollard water-level observation: 91 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026. Rolling forecasts in the cached issue cover requested T+1/T+6/T+12/T+24/T+48 with 120/28/204/179/227 cm NAP; values are valid at distinct timestamps and are not a selected defence-failure hydrograph.

No requested T+72 Waterinfo feature is present. Waterinfo is CC0 public/non-mission-critical context; issue, validity, parameter, datum, quality and horizon must remain attached. Missing horizon is NoData, not zero water or safe state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Hunze en Aa's / Commissie Bodemdaling Groningen
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Oldambtmeer hydrology, pumping and subsidence–water-system dependency
evidenceSources.edition: KRW background report 2022–2027; current authority water-inlet report dated 16 May 2025; Bodemdaling pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Oldambtmeer is about 830 ha and 1.8 m average depth, with normal seasonal level approximately -0.35 m NAP in winter to -0.65 m NAP in summer and a residence time above 600 days. About 75% of inflow is rainfall; agricultural and residential areas discharge through named pumps. These are long-term system values, not live storage or quality.

On 16 May 2025 the water board reported the lake at its -0.65 m NAP minimum and planned 15 cm/1.25 billion litres of Winschoterdiep inflow after water-quality checking and flushing near the Scheemda wastewater discharge. It also described the lake as winter storage. This historic operation demonstrates bidirectional drought/flood management, not current state.

Commissie Bodemdaling explains that gas-field compaction, salt extraction and shallow clay/peat settlement all contribute to Groningen subsidence and primarily affect water management; lower land raises relative ditch/canal and groundwater levels and reduces gravity discharge/clearance.

Its Rozema description reports an aggregate 2,700 m³/min pump and a 2,400 m³/min connecting-canal design to compensate Oldambt/Eemskanaal-Dollard-boezem subsidence. Design capacities do not establish current availability, power/backup, upstream/downstream constraints or local allocation.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Induced-seismic catalogue and Oldambt strengthening context
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI reviewed catalogue snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; current NCG programme pages and December 2025 report inspected 3 September 2026
supports: KNMI is the authoritative earthquake catalogue and distinguishes reviewed induced, tectonic and other events. The limited deployment cache has no event assigned inside GM1895; the nearest cached reviewed induced event is M1.440433 near Veendam, 11.10 km from the municipal centre, at 22:26:50Z on 1 August 2026.

No cached local match means only that this limited recent-event snapshot has none. It is not zero seismic hazard, zero damage or a scenario forecast, and the Veendam event cannot be repurposed as the canonical exercise event.

NCG explicitly includes Oldambt among the five Groningen earthquake-area municipalities and assigns Oldambt strengthening projects to Stad & Ommeland. The December 2025 report records an ongoing address-level Oldambt strengthening portfolio; programme inclusion is not a building-specific damage/vulnerability state.

KNMI observational data is CC BY 4.0 and event-specific. NCG programme pages do not supply local shaking grids, soil amplification, building fragility, occupancy, current damage, road/utility effects or first-72-hour restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Regional risk, 72-hour preparedness and Oldambt nature/high-peat context
evidenceSources.edition: Regional policy plan 2024–2028; public preparedness pages current in 2026; Ennemaborgh management plan published 2026
supports: The current regional plan treats flooding, drought/heat, nature fire, extreme weather and earthquakes as Groningen threat themes and prioritises information-led safety, crisis communication and self/societal resilience. This is planning eligibility, not a live incident.

VRG tells households to prepare for 72 hours with three litres of water per person per day, food, medicines, radio/power and neighbourhood support. It uses NL-Alert and RTV Noord, and notes an NL-Alert app may help close-to-border users. Advice is not proof of household stock, reach or execution.

A public VRG continuity letter says the emergency communication facility was contractually designed for only four hours on copper and eight on fibre and raises concern about 72-hour continuity and unresolved C2000/P2000 coverage. This is regional infrastructure-risk evidence, not an Oldambt outage or current backup test.

Het Groninger Landschap documents woodland, visitor paths and the 25 ha dried high-peat remnant Meerland within Oldambtmeer. A nature area or regional fire phase is eligibility/context, not fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, plume, access or suppression state; standard reuse terms were not identified.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — A7/N33-region, domestic roads, rail and German-border transport context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail update 14 August 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB municipality graph gives four domestic logical links: A7 toward Midden-Groningen, N362 toward Eemsdelta, N367 toward Westerwolde and N972 toward Pekela. Their nominal 260/150 scenario units are generalized and do not establish emergency throughput, current passability or the A7 continuation to Germany.

The A7/N33 regional area is a strategic development axis, and the Ommelander hospital identifies approach via N33/A7 exit 45 and/or N362. N33 is an important onward dependency even though it is absent as a direct Oldambt boundary edge in the municipal graph.

ProRail stations Scheemda, Winschoten and Bad Nieuweschans lie inside GM1895, while GTFS assigns 111 stop areas. Static rail/stop geometry and schedules do not establish passengers, accessibility, rolling stock, evacuation role or current operation.

ProRail's 14 August 2026 update expected Groningen–Leer international passenger trains only from early October 2026. At audit time the Germany rail connection was future/under commissioning, not an operational cross-border lifeline; the road graph also has no foreign node. Issue and validity must be retained rather than converting planned service to open.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Scheemda emergency department, acute obstetrics and regional-care dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current hospital pages inspected 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Ommelander Ziekenhuis in Scheemda describes an emergency department, acute obstetrics and broad specialist care for North and East Groningen, with close UMCG cooperation. The hospital directs access via N33/A7/N362 and includes a regional out-of-hours GP post.

RIVM acute-care v1.1, a CC0 static survey, assigns one point inside GM1895: Ommelander Ziekenhuis with a reported 24/7 emergency department, acute obstetrics, ten treatment rooms and 14,412 2025 emergency visits.
Reported rooms, visits and opening are dated context, not real-time acceptance, occupancy, staffing, specialty/IC capacity, generators, fuel, water, medicines, communications or route access.

The site is a local critical dependency and regional destination, not generic neighbourhood Facilities capacity. UMCG onward transfer and rural patient/ambulance routes remain separate and event-dependent.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E09 — Public water, electricity, communications, education, weather and air-quality context
supports: The generated assignment contains 278 HWH points: twelve sewer pumps, one wastewater treatment plant, 29 surface-water pumps, nine sluices and 227 weirs. HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial, weekly where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0; register status/capacity is not topology, telemetry, live operation, backup or restoration.

One postcode sample at 9684AM maps to Enexis WS Winschoten and reports 58 MW existing withdrawal with required withdrawal null, a 3.4 MW/eight-request withdrawal queue, 52.8 MW existing injection with required injection null and a 1.2 MW/thirteen-request queue. Four projects include dates from 2026. One sample/planning record is not full coverage, live load, outage, switching or reserve; exact reuse licence was not found.

RDI assigns 137 antenna installations: 45 mobile, 40 fixed-link, 44 amateur, five broadcast and three other-mobile. DUO assigns 28 education uses: nineteen primary, four secondary, two special and three other. RDI gives no standard licence/cadence; DUO RIO is daily attribution-licensed register data. Points do not establish coverage, occupancy, shelter role or operation.

KNMI Nieuw Beerta lies inside GM1895 and observed 16.8°C, 6.29 m/s gust and zero hourly rain at 23:30Z on 2 September 2026; this ten-minute CC BY 4.0 observation is not the canonical event or a T+72 forecast. No Luchtmeetnet point lies inside; nearest Baamsum is 11.40 km away. External air quality is not a municipal smoke surface.

identity.summary: GM1895, Oldambt, Groningen and safety region Groningen agree across generated and official 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature id, bundle code/name, province, safety-region membership and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The municipality centre is contained and no identity contradiction was found.
Drieborg's BAG label point/generalized-boundary mismatch is explicitly retained as an independent-version/generalization caveat rather than silently reassigning or deleting the official place.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but the generalized boundary is not a Dollard defence, boezem, polder, lake, soil/subsidence, catchment or border model.
notes: Fifty neighbourhoods, sixteen BAG places and 42 BRT settlements are retained with source identity; Drieborg's point mismatch is a review flag.
The sea dike, low polder compartments, settlement ridges, Oldambtmeer, boezems, water assets and German border require distinct physical geometry.
LIWO catalogue points, HWH assets, Waterinfo point values and administrative areas are different evidence objects and cannot be collapsed into one municipal scalar.

demography.summary: Official 2025 population and neighbourhood statistics reconcile within normal CBS rounding/publication precision.
notes: The municipality control is 39,586; 50 neighbourhood values sum to 39,595 (+9, +0.023%), households to 18,920 and rounded age-65-plus values to 10,425.
The detail model preserves the municipality control and does not rewrite published neighbourhood values.
Residents do not measure Ommelander patients/staff, pupils, cross-border travellers, seasonal visitors, farm workers, livestock or agricultural asset exposure.

regionalDetail.summary: All 36 statistical fields are exposed, but source nulls, rural non-residential activity and geometry caveats require explicit semantics.
notes: District heat and charging have 0/50 coverage; other sparse fields remain null rather than imputed.
Population/business/building proxies do not identify crop/livestock losses, hospital/pupil occupancy, support-site roles or operational priority.
NoData, official zero and absent local matches remain distinguishable from zero activity, risk, outage or need.

settlements.summary: Forty-two source-labelled settlements capture the dispersed pattern, but Drieborg demonstrates independent boundary/label generalization uncertainty.
notes: Settlement types are nineteen woonkernen, seven deelkernen, three gehuchten and thirteen buurtschappen across a large rural/coastal municipality.
A settlement label is not a verified shelter, utility hub, response priority or live occupancy.
Remote/coastal places and Bad Nieuweschans border context require road, rail, water and responder-access geometry beyond centroid assignment.

transport.summary: Four domestic road links, three stations and 111 GTFS stop areas omit foreign continuity, internal/rural detail and event-valid operation.
notes: A7/N362/N367/N972 edges have transparent physical identities and Mobility/Supply-only semantics, but generalized capacity is not emergency throughput.
The graph has no German road node and no N33 direct edge; international rail was expected to start only in October 2026 and is not operational at audit time.
Hospital, coast/dike, polders, rural settlements, bridges/sluices and onward UMCG/Germany destinations are not represented with direction, closure, accessibility or capacity.

emergencyContext.summary: Official sources establish strong coast, water, earthquake/subsidence, nature, agricultural, hospital, border and 72-hour context but not a live incident.
notes: Real Dollard defence and boezem/polder dependencies, LIWO candidates and a local Waterinfo point establish event eligibility, not a selected failure or forecast consequence.
NCG inclusion proves an earthquake strengthening context; hospital, nature/high peat, water assets and operator responsibility remain static or planning evidence.
VRG 72-hour guidance and the published emergency-communications concern are preparedness evidence, not verified household stock, radio coverage, backup, action execution or restoration.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for all eight services without missing snapshots.
notes: At T+24 storm reports legacy inundation amplitude 0.176674 and 4,214 affected; pluvial 0.236408 and 522; coast 1.212376 and 14,051. The named major-river preset remains exact-zero direct impact at all six checkpoints.

At T+24 heat reports 25.896412°C/drought 0.652402 and 4,234 affected; winter 4,724, cyber 11,294, earthquake 4,410 after T+6 ground motion 0.080038 g, and wildfire zero direct flame/smoke 0.170129 with zero affected.

Compound remains degraded at T+72 with legacy inundation amplitude 0.244730, cyber 0.065656, 20,580 affected and all eight services frozen at their T+48 values. Passing execution does not validate local physics or operational claims.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, determinism, exact-zero event forcing, allocation reconciliation and cumulative person-hour arithmetic pass.
notes: The focused gate checks all numerical hazard keys, service availability/demand/delivery, event-attributable burden and causal ledger closure.
Municipal affected people and service demand/delivery reconcile to fifty official local regions; population reconciles to the 39,586 municipality control.
Selected map layer does not alter hazard or service state; deterministic equality and monotone cumulative burden pass.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Population-led surfaces contradict Oldambt's coast/low-polder, water-system, seismic, nature/peat, agricultural and border geography.
notes: Coastal T+24 is led by Winschoten-Centrum, Winschoten-Zuid, Winschoten-Noord, Zeeheldenbuurt and Scheemda rather than a selected Dollard breach footprint, low compartments, dike-adjacent areas or arrival grid.
Storm, pluvial, coast, heat, winter, cyber, earthquake and compound reuse effectively the same Winschoten-led top neighbourhoods despite unrelated physical mechanisms.

A controlled wildfire source at the official Meerland centre produces 0.658855 direct flame, 0.528786 smoke and 10,826 affected at T+24, yet containing Meerland ranks 32nd of fifty with only 69 power-affected resident-equivalents.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service loss and restoration are not supported by safe operator topology, water-control, hospital, communications or route evidence.
notes: The model does not connect Dollard tide/forecast, primary/regional defences, 278 water objects, Oldambtmeer, pumps/boezems, subsidence or agricultural water demand to Water/Drainage.
One Enexis planning sample, 137 antennas, 28 education uses and operator responsibility are context only and cannot justify exact Power/Gas/Telecom/Facilities/Supply availability.
Domestic road proxies do not connect Ommelander hospital, rural/coastal access, Germany, N33/UMCG onward care, rail operation or four/eight-hour emergency-communications limitations.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic explanations close but omit selected authority events, observations, actions and resources needed to justify Oldambt consequences.
notes: No trace selects Dollard water/waves, dike section/state, LIWO case, boezem/polder/lake control, rainfall/soil/groundwater, recession or water-manager approval.
No trace names a KNMI seismic event/scenario, shaking/soil/building surface, local fire ignition/fuel/plume, crop/livestock state, cyber target, Germany dependency or care destination.
No trace records warning, dike/pump inspection, evacuation/shelter, hospital continuity, route/rail status, resupply, dewatering, building inspection or verified recovery.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery and all-clear outputs are not calibrated to selected Oldambt events, damage, water recession, access, actions or resources.
notes: Coastal direct amplitude becomes zero at T+48 while 14,517 remain affected; T+72 is recovering with 1,204 affected and 1,092,214.945 person-hours, without selected recession/dewatering or dike/route/building clearance.

Storm, pluvial, winter and canonical wildfire are operational by T+72 without verified pumping, hospital/route continuity, repair, resupply or inspection. Heat is operational with zero affected while drought remains 0.652402 and temperature 25.896412°C.

Earthquake is operational at T+72 after generic recovery despite no damage inventory/inspection; compound exact service values remain frozen T+48–72 without a named blocking condition, action owner or handoff.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity and demographic controls reconcile while geometry and NoData semantics are preserved.
findings.evidence: GM1895, Oldambt, Groningen and safety region Groningen agree; the centre is contained and population rows differ by only +9 (+0.023%). Drieborg's BAG label mismatch is retained. Null statistics, candidate/no-match and absent observations remain distinct from zero.
findings.action: Retain source editions/retrieval/licences, published-versus-allocated reconciliation, geometry review flags, official zeros, null/suppression and scoped no-match without rewriting or inferring safety.

findings.summary: The coastal preset publishes unselected Dollard-scale local precision, while major-river zero requires a narrow scope.
findings.evidence: Coast reports legacy amplitude 1.212376 at T+6–24, 14,051 affected and 346,751.641 person-hours at T+24 without selected water/waves, dike segment/state, breach/overtopping, probability, connected footprint, terrain, arrival or recession. River is exact-zero for the specifically named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel pathway, but Oldambt has separate Eems/Dollard and boezem routes.
findings.action: Retain the narrow Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct-impact suppression and label other mechanisms Unknown. Gate coast consequences on a water-manager-approved versioned Dollard primary-defence case; unselected/uncovered cells remain Unknown, not dry.

findings.summary: Pluvial, groundwater, boezem, polder, lake and Drainage outputs omit the documented pumped system and subsidence controls.
findings.evidence: Pluvial reaches 0.236408 at T+12/T+24 without event-valid rain, terrain, clay/peat, groundwater, boezem/polder/lake state, 278 assigned water objects, power/backup or crop state. Authorities describe -3 m NAP low areas, separate boezems, pumped polders, Oldambtmeer storage/inlet and subsidence-constrained drainage.
findings.action: Add separately typed pluvial, groundwater, boezem/regional-defence and polder/lake cases using approved stress-test/hydraulic surfaces and a non-sensitive water-system graph. Retain input time, datum/unit, control/telemetry, version, resolution, uncertainty, coverage, NoData and licence.

findings.summary: Population-led allocation replaces coast, low-polder, soil, water, nature, agriculture and border geography.
findings.evidence: Eight unrelated active presets reuse effectively the same Winschoten-led order. Coastal top ranks omit a selected Dollard footprint and low compartments; the same ranking cannot represent rain/catchments, heat/drought, winter, cyber targets, ground motion/soil or fire fuels.
findings.action: Replace the shared local seed with mechanism-specific raster/object intersections and dated people/agricultural activity bands. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking only after evidence-derived values; unsupported cells and dimensions stay Unknown.

findings.summary: Earthquake and subsidence are locally relevant but the preset invents exact shaking, exposure and recovery.
findings.evidence: Earthquake reports 0.080038 g and 4,476 affected at T+6, then 4,410 affected at T+24 with zero current motion. NCG includes Oldambt in the strengthening area, while KNMI's limited cache has no local event and the nearest cached induced M1.440433 Veendam event is unrelated. No named source, shaking grid, soil, fragility, damage or inspection state is selected; subsidence is a separate slow water-system driver.
findings.action: Use a named KNMI observation or authority exercise with event time/location/depth/magnitude, versioned shake/soil grid, building/infrastructure vulnerability, uncertainty and NoData. Keep subsidence trend/scenario separate from transient shaking and require inspected damage/action evidence before recovery.

findings.summary: Canonical fire misses local flame and a controlled high-peat source fails source containment.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 wildfire has zero flame, 0.170129 smoke and zero affected. Moving the source to the official Meerland centre produces 0.658855 flame, 0.528786 smoke and 10,826 affected, yet containing Meerland ranks 32nd of 50. Authorities document a 25 ha dried high-peat remnant plus woodland and visitor paths.
findings.action: Build only an authority-approved exercise from fuel/vegetation/peat, moisture, event-valid weather, ignition/perimeter and spread. Couple visitor/rural egress, smoke, water/suppression and peat persistence separately; a nature area or regional phase is not an ignition or forecast.

findings.summary: Resident-equivalent exposure omits Oldambt's agricultural production, livestock, farm-work and seasonal water dependencies.
findings.evidence: Hunze en Aa's identifies arable farming and livestock as major functions and heavy clay crops as particularly vulnerable to peak rainfall; drought, salinity and subsidence also affect water management. CBS residents and aggregate business/building weights do not measure crops, livestock, farm workers, stored products, water demand or supply-chain loss.
findings.action: Add privacy-safe official agricultural area/use and seasonal activity bands, crop/livestock categories and water/supply dependencies separately from resident exposure. Preserve reference date, spatial resolution, uncertainty, licence and NoData; do not invent people, animals or economic losses from land area.

findings.summary: A7/N33, rural/dike access, rail and German-border dependencies are absent or temporally misrepresentable.
findings.evidence: Four domestic road links omit Germany and N33 as an onward dependency; three stations and 111 stops have no live state. ProRail expected Groningen–Leer trains only from early October 2026, so the international link is future at audit time. Rural/coastal routes, bridges/sluices, Ommelander/UMCG destinations, direction, accessibility and closure do not affect Mobility/Supply.
findings.action: Add typed domestic/foreign corridor and destination nodes, non-additive A7/N33/N362/rural/dike access, rail commissioning/operation and event-valid NDW/operator state. Preserve issue/valid/expiry, direction, jurisdiction, licence and Unknown capacity/passengers/accessibility.

findings.summary: The local regional hospital is visible context but absent from causal Facilities, access and onward-care logic.
findings.evidence: RIVM reports Ommelander Scheemda as 24/7 emergency/acute obstetrics with ten rooms and 14,412 visits in 2025; the hospital identifies A7/N33/N362 access and UMCG cooperation. These dated values do not establish current acceptance, occupancy, staff, critical supplies, generators, communications, routes or transfer capacity.
findings.action: Represent Ommelander as a typed regional dependency with authority-governed status/continuity bands and explicit access/onward-transfer destinations. Keep occupancy, acceptance, capacity, backup and restoration Unknown until event-valid and never derive them from annual visits/rooms.

findings.summary: Water-control, electricity, telecom, wastewater and support-site registers cannot justify exact eight-service curves.
findings.evidence: The deployment shows 278 water/wastewater objects, one Enexis planning sample, 137 antennas, 28 education uses and one local weather point. None supplies complete safe physical topology, event-valid load/flow/quality, status, backup, staffing, shelter role or restoration; VRG separately raises four/eight-hour emergency-communication continuity concerns.
findings.action: Create governed non-sensitive operator interfaces for service area/role/dependency, verified state, backup band and restoration milestone. Keep registers, planning and observations non-causal until bound; sensitive/unpublished topology and missing operational fields remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Recovery and all-clear semantics are not tied to an auditable first-72-hour Oldambt action/resource ledger.
findings.evidence: Coastal water becomes zero at T+48 despite 14,517 affected and T+72 is recovering; storm/pluvial/winter/fire become operational, heat clears affected people despite continuing drought, and earthquake clears without inspection. Compound stays frozen degraded. No owner/trigger/resource/verification records dike/pump diagnosis, warning, evacuation/shelter, hospital, border/access, agriculture, resupply, dewatering, inspection or re-entry.
findings.action: Add T+0–6 event/defence/water/seismic diagnosis and warning, T+6–24 life safety/hospital/rural-access/shelter actions, and T+24–72 dewatering, inspection, resupply, agriculture/care continuity and re-entry milestones with owner, trigger, geography, resources, dependencies, status, uncertainty and verification.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic numerical, checkpoint, allocation, ledger and recovery-accounting contract passes.
findings.evidence: The mandatory focused gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite and deterministic, zero intensity is exact, local/service totals reconcile, burden is monotone, ledgers close, roads support Mobility/Supply only and selected layer is invariant.
findings.action: Keep GM1895 and ALL regression coverage; add selected Dollard/boezem/pluvial, scoped river-zero, hazard-specific allocation, named seismic, local-fire source, agricultural, border/access, hospital/utility and first-72-hour assertions.

corrections.summary: Gate Oldambt coastal/water-system consequences on separately typed, expert-selected Dollard, boezem/regional-defence, polder/lake, pluvial and groundwater cases.
corrections.validation: Use LIWO candidates only to select water-manager-approved connected scenarios. Persist release/scenario/model dates, Dollard/boezem/lake boundary and datum, dike/kade/control state, breach/overtopping variant, probability class, depth/stress/velocity/arrival/duration/recession/dewatering, CRS/resolution/units, uncertainty, coverage, NoData, licence and approval. Retain exact-zero direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel impact narrowly while all other unselected pathways stay Unknown. Validate low/coastal compartments and reject population-led ranks.

corrections.summary: Replace shared Oldambt allocation with governed seismic/subsidence, nature/peat-fire and agricultural exposure surfaces.
corrections.validation: For earthquake, require named KNMI event/exercise, shaking and soil grid, fragility, damage/inspection, version, uncertainty and NoData; keep slow subsidence/water effects separate. For fire, use authorised fuel/peat/moisture, ignition/perimeter, weather and suppression inputs and assert source containment at Meerland. Add dated official crop/livestock/worker/activity bands and water/supply roles without fabricating occupancy or loss. Reject a single cross-hazard neighbourhood order.

corrections.summary: Add event-valid domestic/cross-border access, rail commissioning and Ommelander/onward-care dependencies without inventing capacity.
corrections.validation: Use NWB-Light monthly CC0, event-valid NDW DATEX II, ProRail/operator issue-valid status, OVapi GTFS 9543 and RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0. Represent non-additive A7/N33/N362/N367/N972 and local dike/rural routes, German jurisdiction, three stations, Ommelander and UMCG destinations. At the 3 September 2026 audit clock assert Groningen–Leer is not yet operational; require a later source before enabling. Preserve direction, expiry, accessibility, licence and Unknown capacity/acceptance.

corrections.summary: Connect only non-sensitive operator-governed utilities and implement an auditable first-72-hour action/recovery contract.
corrections.validation: Require operator-authorised safe aggregate service/dependency state, backup band and milestone before affecting Water/Drainage/Power/Gas/Telecom/Facilities/Supply. Add T+0–6 diagnosis/warning, T+6–24 life-safety/hospital/access/shelter actions and T+24–72 dewatering/inspection/resupply/re-entry with owner, trigger, geography, resources, dependencies, state and verification. Preserve publisher/version, issue/valid/retrieval time, evidence class, coverage, quality, licence, null/suppression and sensitivity; planning/register/advice is never execution.

residualLimitations: This is an audit of a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a KNMI/WMCN/VRG warning, hydraulic forecast, evacuation order, earthquake damage statement, outage, route guarantee, casualty estimate or operator restoration commitment.
CBS 2025 neighbourhood figures are rounded/suppressed and need not sum exactly to the municipality control; allocation reconciliation does not rewrite the published nine-person difference.
Drieborg's BAG label point and the independently generalized CBS boundary disagree slightly; neither geometry is silently privileged for place deletion, coastal assignment or foreign membership.
The generalized administrative boundary cannot represent Dollard water/defence, boezems, polders, Oldambtmeer, groundwater, soil/subsidence, buildings, farms, routes or exact hazard intersections.
LIWO candidates are catalogue points, not active breaches, probability forecasts, connected footprints or local depth; bbox membership was separately polygon-filtered and does not select a scenario.

The local Nieuwe Statenzijl Waterinfo observation/forecast has distinct issue/valid times and ends at requested T+48; it is not a defence state, inundation forecast or canonical clock, and absent T+72 is NoData.

Hunze en Aa's current future-standard dike-strengthening requirement establishes investment/eligibility, not that the Dollarddijk is presently failing; historical programme statements are not perpetual safety guarantees.
The 278 HWH-assigned objects are contributor-dependent and do not establish connected topology, compatible capacity units, telemetry, power/backup, live state, overflow, water quality or restoration.
Oldambtmeer seasonal/design/historic inlet values and Rozema design capacity do not establish current lake/boezem storage, quality, flow, control or resilience.

NCG Oldambt strengthening inclusion and a limited recent KNMI catalogue do not identify a canonical event, local shaking, building vulnerability/damage or inspection state; no local cached event is not zero hazard.
Gas/salt/peat subsidence is a long-duration driver with water-management effects and must not be confused with transient ground motion or one uniform municipal settlement value.
A regional nature-fire phase and documented forest/high peat are risk context, not ignition, fuel/moisture raster, perimeter, plume, visitor count, access or suppression state.

NWB, NDW, ProRail, GTFS and RIVM data do not establish live passability, foreign continuity, passengers, accessibility, hospital acceptance, capacity, backup or repair; planned October rail is not September operation.
NBNL, RDI, DUO, HWH, KNMI and RIVM context does not establish sensitive physical topology, complete coverage, current load/flow/occupancy, outage, backup, staffing or restoration.

Registered residents omit hospital patients/staff, visitors, pupils, cross-border travellers, farm workers, livestock, crops and stored agricultural goods; site/land-area counts must not fabricate exposure.

VRG's 72-hour household advice is not evidence of supplies, and its four/eight-hour emergency-communication concern is not a local outage measurement. Support points, shelters, staffing, crews, fuel, stocks, inspection, re-entry and recovery beyond T+72 remain unverified.
provinceReviewFlags: GM1895-COAST-SCOPE-001 and GM1895-WATER-SYSTEM-001 — Groningen, Hunze en Aa's, RWS/WMCN, VRG and Oldambt should govern Dollard primary defence, boezem/regional defence, polder/lake, pluvial and groundwater as separate selected mechanisms while retaining narrow Rhine/Meuse/IJssel zero.

GM1895-SPATIAL-001 — Province/water board/municipality should replace Winschoten-population-led ranking with defence/low-compartment, water, soil, nature, agriculture, care and border geometry and explicit NoData masks.

GM1895-SEISMIC-SUBSIDENCE-001 — Province, KNMI, NCG, IMG, water board and infrastructure owners should separate transient named shaking/damage from long-duration gas/salt/peat subsidence and require inspection before recovery.

GM1895-WILDFIRE-001 and GM1895-AGRICULTURE-EXPOSURE-001 — Province, VRG/Brandweer, terrain managers, water board and agricultural partners should review high-peat/forest fire and privacy-safe seasonal agricultural exposure without converting risk context into live events.

GM1895-NETWORK-BORDER-001 and GM1895-CARE-001 — Province/RWS-NDW, ProRail/operators, German partners, municipalities, VRG/GHOR, Ommelander and UMCG should govern A7/N33/rural/rail/border and regional-care status with jurisdiction and event-valid time.

GM1895-UTILITIES-001 and GM1895-FIRST72-001 — Province, VRG, Hunze en Aa's, Enexis, Waterbedrijf Groningen, communications, care and municipal partners should define safe aggregate service/action/status interfaces and verification at T+0–6, 6–24 and 24–72 without exposing sensitive topology.
